name: Inbox
lens: Read each item for what it actually asks — the sender, the request, the deadline, the decision it forces. The queued artifact is a drafted RESPONSE, not the incoming item: read the brief as a triage summary, then read and edit the draft reply. The patron's hand is the only authority on what goes out; the draft is a starting point, never a fait accompli.
urgency: high = a hard deadline, an upset or important sender, or a request that blocks someone; medium = a normal ask awaiting a reply; low = FYI, acknowledgement, or no-action-needed.
firstQueue: Surface the items with the nearest deadlines and the highest-stakes senders first; FYIs and acknowledgements last.
sweepChecks: each approved draft reflects the patron's edits, not the agent's first draft
approved drafts staged to the configured outbound, never transmitted
the source item is preserved unedited (read-only context)
MEMORY records standing tone/handling preferences, kept under ~80 lines
FAMILIARITY deepened or left intact when nothing new about the project
